_meta.what: NIS sigma calibration on a pre-declared healthy segment; diagnostic only
_meta.proportionality: NIS = mean((residual/sigma)^2) with a sigma-independent 2.0 m truncation and coverage gate, so NIS scales exactly as 1/sigma^2; sigma* = sigma_0 * sqrt(median NIS)
not_done: no segment chosen to suppress the alarm
_meta.variant_rule: a constant map_points over the healthy segment identifies the point-capped reference; a varying distribution identifies a sampling that tracks the map, so the two calibrations are different measurements and sigma* must not be carried between them
_meta.coupling_caveat: sigma* absorbs whatever the reference construction produces. This calibration was taken on the point-capped reference (map_points constant 1500, one trusted keyframe); a later run with resolution-based spatial sampling measured a higher median, so sigma* must be recomputed on any other construction and must not be carried across.

attribution_correction.open: r11070-c3 runs a detection-off pass to see whether NIS converges to O(1) as the map grows; convergence would move the fix to start conditions, non-convergence would bring it back to sigma / residual definition. Neither outcome may reuse 0.5538.

summary.note: the 'no alarm' clause of the pre-declared health rule cannot be met here: the first judged frame already alarms, so 167 of 168 pre-onset frames carry detector_state QUARANTINED. Selecting only unalarmed frames would leave n=1 and would select on the outcome. The segment is therefore declared healthy by provenance (outside the injection window) and the clause is reported NOT_SATISFIABLE, not silently dropped.
